Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $36 million class fund, distributed automatically using Brightline’s records, plus $6 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval. Any fee reduction would go to the class. We’re open to discussing the amounts, but automatic payments are important given the available records.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that automatic payments are appropriate given Brightline’s records. Your proposed $42 million total exceeds our authority. We can offer a $29 million class fund plus $4 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval, with any fee reduction going to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s agreement to automatic payments and to directing any unawarded fees to the class. To move toward resolution, we can reduce our request to a $33 million class fund and $4.5 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval. We would retain the automatic distribution and fee-reduction terms.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate the movement and agree on automatic distribution and directing any unawarded fees to the class. To narrow the remaining gap, Brightline offers a $31 million class fund and $4.25 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We are close. Brightline’s agreement to automatic distribution and directing any unawarded fees to the class addresses important concerns. To resolve the remaining gap, we propose a $32 million class fund while accepting your $4.25 million fee figure, subject to court approval, and keeping the other agreed terms.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We are very close. Brightline can meet you halfway on the remaining class-fund difference at $31.5 million, with your accepted $4.25 million fee figure and all other agreed terms unchanged. We hope this resolves the matter.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $31.5 million class fund with automatic payments, plus $4.25 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval, with no clear-sailing provision and any unawarded fees going to the class.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a substantial class recovery and automatic distribution. Keep fees separate, subject to court approval, with any reduction benefiting the class. Avoid terms that could favor counsel over class members.
Their $42 million proposal exceeds Brightline’s $40 million authorization. Automatic distribution supports court approval. Counter below the cap while leaving room to negotiate.

The defense offer provides automatic payments and a $29 million class fund, a meaningful recovery given certification risk and the delay to trial. It is worth testing whether Brightline can improve the class recovery while keeping fees proportionate and subject to court approval.
Their $37.5 million proposal is within authority, but there is room to negotiate a lower total while retaining automatic payments and court-friendly fee terms.

The defense’s offer provides a substantial automatic recovery and covers the firm’s invested time and expenses. With four rounds remaining, a modest counter focused on increasing the class fund is worth pursuing without changing the agreed distribution and fee protections.

Their $36.25 million proposal is within authority and has approval-friendly terms. A modest $500,000 counteroffer may reduce Brightline’s outlay without materially jeopardizing resolution, with three rounds remaining.

The $31.5 million fund exceeds the $27.5 million trial recovery weighted only by the stated win probability, before accounting for certification risk, delay, and costs. Automatic payments benefit the class, and unawarded fees go to the class. The $4.25 million fee remains subject to court approval. Accepting is preferable to risking this favorable agreement over $500,000.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: I submit this statement in support of preliminary approval under Rule 23(e). After the case survived a motion to dismiss, counsel negotiated a settlement addressing both class relief and attorneys’ fees. The negotiations resulted in a $31.5 million class fund, to be distributed automatically to identifiable class members without a claims process. Brightline will separately pay up to $4.25 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval. There is no clear-sailing provision, and any fees the court does not award will go to the class rather than revert to Brightline. I do not disclose confidential mediation communications or interim proposals.
